newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM'S PARTY HOLDS SLIGHT LEAD OVER OPPOSITION.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM'S PARTY HOLDS SLIGHT LEAD OVER OPPOSITION.

text.p: Czech Prime Minster Vaclav
Klaus's ODS party continues to hold a slim lead over the
leading opposition Social Democrats just one month before
nationwide Senate elections, a poll released on Monday showed.
The October poll, conducted by the state-run Institute for
Public Opinion Research (IVVM) put Klaus's centre-right Civic
Democratic Party (ODS) at 27 percent among the 1,132 polled, up
two percentage points from an IVVM poll in September.
Meanwhile, the centre-left Social Deomcrats (CSSD) also
gained support, edging up to 25 percent, one point than in the
previous poll.
A September poll, conducted by private Factum agency, also
showed the two parties were running neck-and-neck, giving CSSD
24.4 percent support, while 23.7 percent would vote for ODS.
Elections for the Senate, the upper house of the Czech
parliament, will be held for the first time in the country's
history on November 15-16, under a first past-the-post system
in 81 constituencies.
In parliamentary elections to the lower house at the
beginning of June, CSSD posted a surprisingly strong second
place showing, trailing first place ODS by just over three
percent in the vote, which took away the government's majority
by giving it only 99 seats in the 200-seat body.
Unlike the lower chamber vote, conducted under the
proportional voting system, the Senate elections will use the
majority voting system.
The IVVM poll showed minority coaliton partner the
Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) had slipped slightly to nine
percent from a previous 11 percent but that the Civic
Democratic Alliance (ODA), another coalition partner held
steady at eight percent.
The poll showed the Communist party (KSCM) also stayed even
at nine percent while the far-right Republican Party (SPR-RSC)
would not pass the five percent threshold necessary for winning
seats in the chamber, after winning 8.0 percent in the last
elections.
